summary: Octagonal tower still fitted with its cab, on one side of Little and Big McDougal Lakes; the Firelookout.ca contributor was not sure of the exact spot.

facts.design: Octagonal tower with its cab still in place

evidence.supports: octagonal tower that still has its cab
evidence.quote: It's an octagonal tower that still has its cab.

evidence.supports: tower stands near Little and Big McDougal Lakes; contributor unsure of the exact spot
evidence.quote: I'm not sure if this is the exact spot but the tower almost definitely stands on this side of Little and Big McDougal Lakes.

evidence.supports: most Ontario towers erected 1920s to 1950s, in forest fire protection's heyday
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: towers came under the Department of Lands and Forests, which became the MNR in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: from the 1960s aerial spotting and firefighting crews took over; towers used less
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: the MNR decided in 2013 to remove many standing towers; the fan site does not name the McDougal-Thorne tower
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these towers still standing.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: the only tower-specific source is one undated Firelookout.ca contributor note with no build year, height, staffing or access detail. The brief has no local_unit, so the story gives the region only (Ontario). The contributor was unsure of the exact spot, so the brief coordinates (46.72629, -79.2181) are unverified. A Firelookout.ca Instagram post from March 2023 (seen only as a search result, page not readable) also says the tower has its cab, but it is not cited. A Facebook video linked from the entry was not read. The fan site is cited only for general Ontario context.
